label: History
value: Allan arrived in Avonlea.
unit: Allan arrived in Avonlea as the community's new minister alongside his wife, with the young couple still on their honeymoon at the start of his ministry. During an early visit to Green Gables for tea, he and his wife admired Anne Shirley's decorated table, and Allan engaged in a pleasant conversation with Matthew Cuthbert. Though his wife maintained a warm, supportive presence in the community—comforting Anne after a baking mishap, hosting her at the manse, and later conversing with her about teaching and life goals—Allan remained settled in his role leading the local parish.

Mrs. Allan later invited Anne to tea at the manse, further cementing a friendly rapport where she listens to Anne's thoughts and shares local community news.

Over time, her hairstyle has ranged from short shingled hair and short silky curls to an unbraided torrent of brightness streaming behind her.

label: Personality
value: Anne is extremely talkative.
unit: Extremely talkative, highly imaginative, and prone to daydreaming, this individual possesses a heedless and impulsive nature alongside a remarkable quickness to learn. Driven by strong ambitions, her early motivations center on achieving high examination results to surpass a rival and make her guardians proud, aiming to follow in the footsteps of a beloved teacher. She harbors a deep desire to be loved by everyone, striving to bring joy to others and add beauty to life, while harboring a specific dread of a haunted wood after dark. A talented reciter who excels at handling children, her aspirations expand to pursuing fame through writing short stories, winning the Avery scholarship, and attending college. Later, she dedicates herself to securing the Thorburn Scholarship in English to ensure she can continue her college studies without burdening her guardian's savings.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia
unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia as an orphan girl, Anne Shirley was raised by hand by Mrs. Thomas before living with Mrs. Hammond for over two years. Upon arriving at Green Gables, she was taken in by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert after an initial mix-up. She formed an immediate lifelong friendship with Diana Barry and developed a fierce academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after breaking a slate over his head at school. After attending Queen's Academy and forfeiting her Redmond scholarship to stay at Green Gables following Matthew's death, she taught at Avonlea school and helped found the local Improvement Society. She also took in the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora, alongside Marilla. During this time, Anne accidentally colored her nose bright red with dye and broke through a duck house roof while trying to buy a replacement willow-ware platter. She later attended Redmond College, living at Patty's Place with friends and earning a thousand-dollar legacy from Miss Josephine Barry. While at Redmond, Anne rejected marriage proposals from both Gilbert and the wealthy Roy Gardner, though she later realized her true feelings and accepted Gilbert's proposal in Hester Gray's garden.

Upon arriving at Green Gables, she was taken in by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert after an initial mix-up. She formed an immediate lifelong friendship with Diana Barry and developed a fierce academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after breaking a slate over his head at school. After attending Queen's Academy and forfeiting her Redmond scholarship to stay at Green Gables following Matthew's death, she taught at Avonlea school and helped found the local Improvement Society. She also took in the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora, alongside Marilla. During this time, Anne accidentally colored her nose bright red with dye and broke through a duck house roof while trying to buy a replacement willow-ware platter. She later attended Redmond College, living at Patty's Place with friends and earning a thousand-dollar legacy from Miss Josephine Barry. While at Redmond, Anne rejected marriage proposals from both Gilbert and the wealthy Roy Gardner, though she later realized her true feelings and accepted Gilbert's proposal in Hester Gray's garden.

value: Anne Shirley said: "You would cry, too, if you were an orphan and had come to a place you thought was going to be home and found that they didn’t want you because you weren’t a boy. Oh, this is the most tragical thing that ever happened to me!"

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "but, oh, please do call me Cordelia. It can’t matter much to you what you call me if I’m only going to be here a little while, can it? And Anne is such an unromantic name."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "why didn’t you tell me at the station that you didn’t want me and leave me there? If I hadn’t seen the White Way of Delight and the Lake of Shining Waters it wouldn’t be so hard."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "She brought Lily Jones for herself. Lily is only five years old and she is very beautiful and had nut-brown hair. If I was very beautiful and had nut-brown hair would you keep me?"

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Pretty well. I’m better at looking after children, though. I’ve had so much experience at that. It’s such a pity you haven’t any here for me to look after."

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was named after James.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, James, who drowned at sea a month before her birth. She was given a pet cat, the Sarah-cat, by her washerwoman. She arrived at Patty's Place with her cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, to serve as a chaperone for Anne Shirley, Stella Maynard, Priscilla, and Philippa Gordon. During her time keeping house with the college girls, she offered them her relaxed philosophy on chaperoning and joined in discussions regarding household expenses, beauty, marriage, and potential suitors. At the conclusion of their final examinations, Aunt Jamesina gathered with the girls to reflect on what their four years at Redmond College had taught them before they packed up Patty's Place at the end of their studies.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews drove Anne Shirley to a benefit concert at the White Sands Hotel.
unit: Billy Andrews drove Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews to and from a benefit concert at the White Sands Hotel, where he transported them home under the moonlight. Later, his father gave him the upper farm in his own name. Through his sister Jane, the shy Billy delivered an unromantic marriage proposal by proxy to Anne, which she declined. By the time Anne returned to Avonlea after attending college, Billy had married someone else.

label: History
value: Charlie Sloane grew up as a respectable Avonlea boy.
unit: Charlie Sloane grew up as a respectable Avonlea boy, once fighting Moody Spurgeon MacPherson over a remark about Anne Shirley and telling his mother that Anne was the smartest girl in school. During a farewell party for Anne and Gilbert Blythe before college, Charlie escorted Anne home, though his presence left her regretting the choice. He later traveled with Anne and Gilbert on the journey to Kingsport to begin studies at Redmond College. While at Redmond, Charlie joined Anne, Gilbert, and their friends on social outings, including a walk through the park and Spofford Avenue. During his second term at college, Charlie extended an unwanted proposal of marriage to Anne, which she did not accept.

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth came to live at Echo Lodge.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth came to live at Echo Lodge as a fourteen-year-old servant to Miss Lavendar Lewis. She befriended Anne Shirley during Anne's visits to the cottage and shared her worries about Miss Lavendar's listlessness, which led to Anne helping reunite Miss Lavendar with her old love, Stephen Irving. Charlotta assisted Anne and Diana Barry with the preparations for Miss Lavendar's garden wedding and later helped Anne clean the house after the couple departed. In the following years, Charlotta remained a familiar presence at Echo Lodge, spending time with Anne, Diana, and Paul Irving during their frequent visits.

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "it’s plain to be seen you and Miss Lavendar have got a secret and I think, begging your pardon if I’m too forward, Miss Shirley, ma’am, that it’s real mean not to tell me when we’ve all been such chums."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "But I’m sure I shan’t sleep a blessed wink, Miss Shirley, ma’am, for fear that something’ll go wrong at the last minute . . . the cream won’t whip . . . or Mr. Irving’ll have a stroke and not be able to come."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "but there’s so much to do yet . . . and oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I’m skeered it’s going to rain and I wish you’d get up and tell me you think it ain’t."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "I peeked from the kitchen window . . . and he’s awful handsome . . . and just the right age for Miss Lavendar. And oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, do you think it would be much harm to listen at the door?"

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "Yes, ma’am. Come in, ma’am. I’ll tell Miss Lavendar you’re here, ma’am. She’s upstairs, ma’am."

label: History
value: Davy Keith was an orphan
unit: Davy Keith was an orphan whose father died when he was a baby, and he grew up with little upbringing prior to being taken in at Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert alongside his twin sister, Dora. A mischievous child, Davy quickly established a habit of playing pranks—such as putting a caterpillar down a girl's dress, tricking Dora into a pigpen, and hiding a toad in Marilla's bed—before confiding his antics in Anne Shirley. After he locked Dora in a toolhouse and lied about it, Anne held a heart-to-heart conversation with him to teach him the wrongness of lying. Over time, Davy continued to cause minor chaos, accidentally ruining lemon pies meant for a visiting author and suffering jealousy when Anne spent time with other children. His position at Green Gables was made permanent after his uncle Richard Keith passed away and left money in trust for the twins. When Anne left for Redmond College, Davy stayed behind with Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde, maintaining a close bond with Anne through letters and her holiday visits. During those visits, Davy often relied on Anne to process his misdeeds, confessing to her after lying to Mrs. Lynde to cover up skipping Sunday School to go fishing. As he grew older, Davy continued to entertain Anne with his chatter regarding school, town gossip, and his childhood plans for the future.

A mischievous child, Davy quickly established a habit of playing pranks—such as putting a caterpillar down a girl's dress, tricking Dora into a pigpen, and hiding a toad in Marilla's bed—before confiding his antics in Anne Shirley. After he locked Dora in a toolhouse and lied about it, Anne held a heart-to-heart conversation with him to teach him the wrongness of lying. Over time, Davy continued to cause minor chaos, accidentally ruining lemon pies meant for a visiting author and suffering jealousy when Anne spent time with other children. His position at Green Gables was made permanent after his uncle Richard Keith passed away and left money in trust for the twins. When Anne left for Redmond College, Davy stayed behind with Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde, maintaining a close bond with Anne through letters and her holiday visits. During those visits, Davy often relied on Anne to process his misdeeds, confessing to her after lying to Mrs. Lynde to cover up skipping Sunday School to go fishing. As he grew older, Davy continued to entertain Anne with his chatter regarding school, town gossip, and his childhood plans for the future.

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "You don’t look like a lady who’d whip a little boy just ’cause he couldn’t keep still. Didn’t you find it awful hard to keep still when you was only ‘s old as me?"

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "You was a girl once, I s’pose, though it’s awful funny to think of it. Dora can sit still . . . but there ain’t much fun in it I don’t think. Seems to me it must be slow to be a girl. Here, Dora, let me liven you up a bit."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "Marilla washed it yesterday . . . and Mrs. Wiggins scoured me with hard soap the day of the funeral. That’s enough for one week. I don’t see the good of being so awful clean. It’s lots more comfable being dirty."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "But it was such a jolly big caterpillar . . . I picked him up on the church steps just as we went in. It seemed a pity to waste him. And say, wasn’t it fun to hear that girl yell?"

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “I . . . did something else today,” went on Davy in a muffled voice. “I’m sorry now but I’m awful scared to tell you. You won’t be very cross, will you? And you won’t tell Marilla, will you?”

label: History
value: Diana Barry was named by a visiting schoolmaster
unit: Diana Barry was named by a visiting schoolmaster when she was born. Growing up in Avonlea, she formed an intense childhood bond with Anne Shirley, with whom she imagined ghosts in the Haunted Wood, named local spots like Lover's Lane, and belonged to a Story Club. When Anne moved to Green Gables, the two swore a vow of eternal friendship in the Barrys' garden. Despite a temporary separation enforced by her mother, Diana reunited with Anne after Anne saved her baby sister Minnie May from severe croup while their parents were away. Diana participated in local school activities, performing a solo at the Avonlea Christmas concert and later taking part in outings like discovering Hester Gray's garden.

label: History
value: Diana joined Anne
unit: As they grew older, Diana joined Anne in co-founding and canvassing for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Together, they navigated rural adventures, such as attempting to buy a willow-ware platter from Miss Sarah Copp in Spencervale and taking an accidental detour to Echo Lodge to meet Miss Lavendar Lewis. When Anne left for Redmond College while Diana stayed in Avonlea, the two maintained a close correspondence, keeping each other updated on community news, literary efforts, and personal developments. Diana eventually became secretly engaged to Fred Wright, a step that signaled shifting dynamics in their peer group. Shortly before Anne's second year at college, Diana and Fred were married at Orchard Slope with Anne assisting her as a bridesmaid. Following her wedding, Diana settled into her new home in Avonlea and soon gave birth to a baby boy, whom Anne visited during her return home.

Together, they navigated rural adventures, such as attempting to buy a willow-ware platter from Miss Sarah Copp in Spencervale and taking an accidental detour to Echo Lodge to meet Miss Lavendar Lewis. When Anne left for Redmond College while Diana stayed in Avonlea, the two maintained a close correspondence, keeping each other updated on community news, literary efforts, and personal developments. Diana eventually became secretly engaged to Fred Wright, a step that signaled shifting dynamics in their peer group. Shortly before Anne's second year at college, Diana and Fred were married at Orchard Slope with Anne assisting her as a bridesmaid. Following her wedding, Diana settled into her new home in Avonlea and soon gave birth to a baby boy, whom Anne visited during her return home.

value: Diana Barry said: "Gertie Pye actually went and put her milk bottle in my place in the brook yesterday. Did you ever? I don’t speak to her now."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “I don’t believe he’ll find the doctor at Carmody,” sobbed Diana. “I know that Dr. Blair went to town and I guess Dr. Spencer would go too. Young Mary Joe never saw anybody with croup and Mrs. Lynde is away. Oh, Anne!”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “Everything went off very well,” said Diana practically. “I guess we must have made as much as ten dollars. Mind you, Mr. Allan is going to send an account of it to the Charlottetown papers.”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "You’ll ruin your dress in that wet grain . . . ruin it. She doesn’t hear me! Well, she’ll never get that cow out by herself. I must go and help her, of course."

label: Personality
value: Dora is remarkably quiet.
unit: Dora is a remarkably quiet, neat, and faithful child who conducts herself like a model of good behavior. Characterized by her prim and demure manner, she is observant, industrious, and never needs to be told how to do a task twice. She carries out her duties carefully, systematically, and dispassionately, proving to be an exceptionally good and well-behaved child who causes no trouble. Described as placid and composed even in frightening situations, her exceedingly proper and predictable nature can make her seem somewhat monotonous.

During a visit from Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, who were canvassing the area for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society's hall painting fund, Eliza was approached for a contribution. She and her sister dealt with the young women as they successfully secured subscriptions for their cause.

label: Personality
value: Gilbert Blythe is a clever young man.
unit: Gilbert Blythe is a clever and good-natured young man who approaches life with a strong sense of humor, constant good spirits, and a thoughtful, kind demeanor. Driven by a determination to get the best out of life and contribute his best in return, he actively pursues academic excellence, aiming to win a scholarship, achieve High Honors, and earn the Cooper Prize. Professionally, he aspires to become a doctor to do honest work and combat disease, pain, and ignorance. His personal ambitions are deeply shaped by his devotion to Anne Shirley, striving to measure up to her ideal with the ultimate goal of marrying her and building a home together.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea after spending three years in Alberta with his father and visiting cousins in New Brunswick. Upon returning to school, he pulled Anne Shirley's hair and called her "Carrots," prompting her to smash a slate over his head and refuse his attempts to apologize. Over the next few years, Gilbert maintained a intense academic rivalry with Anne while attempting to rescue her when her boat sank, though she initially refused his offer of friendship. After they both earned high marks on the Queen's Entrance examination and attended Queen's Academy together, Gilbert won the medal while Anne earned the Avery scholarship. Upon learning that Anne planned to give up college to care for Marilla following Matthew's death, Gilbert generously gave up his post as the Avonlea schoolteacher so Anne could take the job, which finally led to their reconciliation and close friendship. Together, they founded the Avonlea Young People's Improvement Society and frequently discussed their teaching experiences, literary ambitions, and community projects. Following two years of teaching, Gilbert resigned to attend Redmond College alongside Anne, where he led the Freshmen to victory in the Arts Rush and took High Honors in Classics along with winning the Cooper Prize. During their second year at Redmond, Gilbert met Anne in an orchard and proposed to her, but she rejected his offer of romance and insisted they remain only friends. Crushed by the rejection, Gilbert distanced himself, leaving Anne feeling a lonely ache over his absence while rumors circulated that he was courting Christine Stuart. Years later, after graduating from Redmond, Gilbert fell critically ill with typhoid fever, an event that caused Anne to realize her true love for him. After his fever broke, Gilbert asked Anne to walk with him to Hester Gray's garden, where he proposed a second time, and she happily accepted.

unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea after spending three years in Alberta with his father and visiting cousins in New Brunswick. Upon returning to school, he pulled Anne Shirley's hair and called her "Carrots," prompting her to smash a slate over his head and refuse his attempts to apologize. Over the next few years, Gilbert maintained a intense academic rivalry with Anne while attempting to rescue her when her boat sank, though she initially refused his offer of friendship. After they both earned high marks on the Queen's Entrance examination and attended Queen's Academy together, Gilbert won the medal while Anne earned the Avery scholarship. Upon learning that Anne planned to give up college to care for Marilla following Matthew's death, Gilbert generously gave up his post as the Avonlea schoolteacher so Anne could take the job, which finally led to their reconciliation and close friendship. Together, they founded the Avonlea Young People's Improvement Society and frequently discussed their teaching experiences, literary ambitions, and community projects. Following two years of teaching, Gilbert resigned to attend Redmond College alongside Anne, where he led the Freshmen to victory in the Arts Rush and took High Honors in Classics along with winning the Cooper Prize. During their second year at Redmond, Gilbert met Anne in an orchard and proposed to her, but she rejected his offer of romance and insisted they remain only friends. Crushed by the rejection, Gilbert distanced himself, leaving Anne feeling a lonely ache over his absence while rumors circulated that he was courting Christine Stuart. Years later, after graduating from Redmond, Gilbert fell critically ill with typhoid fever, an event that caused Anne to realize her true love for him. After his fever broke, Gilbert asked Anne to walk with him to Hester Gray's garden, where he proposed a second time, and she happily accepted.

label: History
value: Mr. J. A. Harrison settled in Avonlea
unit: Before settling in Avonlea, Mr. J. A. Harrison spent time on Prince Edward Island as a boy, lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, and kept house with his sister until her death. He put off getting married for a long time before eventually marrying Emily Scott; however, he separated from his wife after a dispute over a parrot named Ginger and relocated to a farm in Avonlea. There, his temper flare-up over a trespassing cow led to an acquaintance with his young neighbor, Anne Shirley, after she accidentally sold his cow instead of her own and came to apologize. Though he initially expressed doubts about Anne's gentle teaching methods and refused to subscribe to her village improvement society, he formed a warm friendship with her over tea and chats about local gossip. A severe hail and thunder storm later devastated Avonlea and killed Ginger, paving the way for a reconciliation when Emily unexpectedly arrived at Green Gables looking for him. After scrubbing his home, Mr. Harrison explained his past separation to Anne, made peace with his wife, and welcomed her back. In subsequent years, he maintained his friendship with Anne, offering critiques of her creative writing and delivering the local mail to Green Gables.

unit: Before settling in Avonlea, Mr. J. A. Harrison spent time on Prince Edward Island as a boy, lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, and kept house with his sister until her death. He put off getting married for a long time before eventually marrying Emily Scott; however, he separated from his wife after a dispute over a parrot named Ginger and relocated to a farm in Avonlea. There, his temper flare-up over a trespassing cow led to an acquaintance with his young neighbor, Anne Shirley, after she accidentally sold his cow instead of her own and came to apologize. Though he initially expressed doubts about Anne's gentle teaching methods and refused to subscribe to her village improvement society, he formed a warm friendship with her over tea and chats about local gossip. A severe hail and thunder storm later devastated Avonlea and killed Ginger, paving the way for a reconciliation when Emily unexpectedly arrived at Green Gables looking for him. After scrubbing his home, Mr. Harrison explained his past separation to Anne, made peace with his wife, and welcomed her back. In subsequent years, he maintained his friendship with Anne, offering critiques of her creative writing and delivering the local mail to Green Gables.

label: Anne Shirley
value: Harrison and Anne first met as neighbors.
unit: Harrison and Anne first met as neighbors on contentious terms when Harrison angrily confronted her over a cow trespassing in his oats. Their friendship truly took root after Anne accidentally sold his Jersey cow by mistake and visited him with a cake peace offering to confess and make amends. Despite Harrison's occasional skepticism regarding her ideas—such as her gentle teaching methods and village improvement projects—the two grew into warm, neighborly friends who frequently shared tea and conversed.

label: History
value: During her schooldays in Avonlea, Jane Andrews belonged to the Story Club.
unit: During her schooldays in Avonlea, Jane Andrews belonged to the Story Club alongside Anne and Ruby Gillis. As she grew older, Jane attended a benefit concert at the White Sands Hotel with Anne and Diana, driven there by her brother Billy. She later prepared to become a teacher, debating methods of school discipline with her peers before taking up a teaching position. During her time in Avonlea, she also participated in the Avonlea Young People's Improvement Society alongside Anne and Diana, visiting local residents to advocate for community improvements. While Anne was attending Redmond College, Jane visited her room one evening to deliver a proxy marriage proposal on behalf of her shy brother Billy; when Anne declined, Jane accepted the refusal with slight coldness before departing the next morning. Jane eventually taught school on the western prairies, and prior to Anne's final year at Redmond, news arrived in Avonlea of Jane's upcoming marriage to a rich man.

label: History
value: Jane attended school.
unit: Jane attended school and Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley, and she had visited the Exhibition twice prior to her studies. While at Queen's Academy taking courses, she visited Anne at her boarding house along with Josie and Ruby to share news about the Avery scholarship to Redmond College. After finishing her studies, Jane joined Anne, Diana, and Priscilla on a springtime walk to Hester Gray's garden, where they spent the afternoon discussing Hester's tragic life and enjoying nature. Over time, her family connection expanded as her brother Billy Andrews married, while she and Ruby Gillis remained topic of conversation among their friends in Avonlea.

label: History
value: Janet Sweet lived at Wayside.
unit: Janet Sweet lived at her charmingly peculiar home, Wayside, in Valley Road, where she welcomed Anne as a boarder. She maintained a twenty-year romance with John Douglas, who routinely walked her home from prayer meetings but failed to propose. After crying on her twentieth anniversary and brief encouragement from Anne to show spirit, Janet briefly rejected John's company, though Anne quickly intervened to reunite them. Following the death of John's mother, John explained that a secret vow to his late mother had prevented him from proposing sooner, leading Janet to forgive the woman and accept his marriage proposal.

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "If she wasn’t—but she is. So we mustn’t speak evil of her. But I’m happy at last, Anne. And I wouldn’t have minded waiting so long a bit if I’d only known why."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "Oh, she does. She’s told me time and again that she’d love to see John settled before her time comes. She’s always giving him hints—you heard her yourself the other day. I thought I’d ha’ gone through the floor."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: “I couldn’t,” said poor Janet pathetically. “You see, Anne, I’ve always been awful fond of John. He might just as well keep coming as not, for there was never anybody else I’d want, so it didn’t matter.”

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "No, I guess not. I was afraid to try, anyway, for fear he’d think I meant it and just go. I suppose I’m a poor-spirited creature, but that is how I feel. And I can’t help it."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: “I dunno,” said Janet hopelessly. “I dunno if I could ever get up enough spunk. Things have drifted so long. But I’ll think it over.”

label: Anne Shirley
value: Janet serves as Anne's hostess.
unit: Janet serves as Anne's hostess when Anne comes to board at her Valley Road home, Wayside. The two become close confidantes who share personal stories and laugh over local suitors, with Anne taking a keen interest in Janet's long-standing romantic troubles. When Janet despairs over her stagnant courtship, Anne encourages her to stand up for herself and later intervenes directly in Janet's love life.

label: History
value: John Henry Carter is known locally as Uncle Abe.
unit: John Henry Carter, known locally as Uncle Abe, made a bold storm prediction that initially served as a source of jokes for Anne and Gilbert. However, his forecast unexpectedly proved accurate when an extraordinarily severe hail and thunder storm struck Avonlea on that exact date. The severe weather caused widespread devastation across the community, damaging homes, destroying crops, killing Mr. Harrison's parrot, and wrecking the trees planted by the Avonlea Improvement Society.

label: History
value: Josephine Barry was an elderly woman.
unit: Josephine Barry was an elderly woman who once paid twenty dollars for a willowware platter and owned a grand house in Charlottetown named Beechwood. She originally intended to cancel Diana Barry's music lessons and leave Avonlea after Anne Shirley and Diana accidentally jumped onto her while she was sleeping in a spare-room bed, but she was won over by Anne's brave apology and candor, becoming close friends with the girl. She subsequently hosted Anne and Diana at Beechwood during the Charlottetown Exhibition and invited Anne to visit her again while Anne attended Queen's Academy. After suffering a dreadful illness for over a year, Miss Barry passed away and left Anne a thousand dollars in her will, which guaranteed Anne the financial security to continue her studies at Redmond College.

She subsequently hosted Anne and Diana at Beechwood during the Charlottetown Exhibition and invited Anne to visit her again while Anne attended Queen's Academy. After suffering a dreadful illness for over a year, Miss Barry passed away and left Anne a thousand dollars in her will, which guaranteed Anne the financial security to continue her studies at Redmond College.

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "Mercy, child, how you have grown! You’re taller than I am, I declare. And you’re ever so much better-looking than you used to be, too. But I dare say you know that without being told."

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself."

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "Oh, I must, hey? I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least. Such carryings on in a respectable house!"

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity."

value: Josie Pye grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Josie Pye grew up in Avonlea, where her mother was a cousin to Aunt Atossa. She attended the local school alongside Anne Shirley and was present among their group of schoolmates when Anne took a dare to walk across a roof. Josie later joined Miss Stacy's advanced class to prepare for the Queen's Entrance examination. After successfully passing, she moved to town to attend Queen's Academy alongside her peers. During their first term, Josie visited Anne's boarding-house room with Jane and Ruby, where they shared the news about the Avery scholarship to Redmond College.

value: Judson Parker planned to rent his fences out for advertisements.
unit: When Judson Parker planned to rent his fences out for advertisements, he initially refused a request from a committee of the Improvement Society—including Anne, Diana, and Jane—to reconsider. Shortly afterward, Anne accidentally overheard Judson accepting a political bribe from Jerry Corcoran near the Lake of Shining Waters. Fearing that Anne would expose the bribe, Judson quickly relented and agreed to pull his advertising agreement, thereby saving the fences from being used for ads.

label: History
value: Lavendar was named by her father.
unit: Named Lavendar by her father for his love of the scent, Miss Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge with her young maid, Charlotta the Fourth, after a quarrel twenty-five years prior severed her engagement to Stephen Irving. After Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally discovered her home, Miss Lavendar befriended them and revealed the story of her past romance. value: Lavendar Lewis said: "But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "to believe I’m old. Now, who are you . . . just for convenience’ sake? Diana Barry? And Anne Shirley? May I pretend that I’ve known you for a hundred years and call you Anne and Diana right away?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I love them myself. They are very good company . . . with a little pretending. On calm evenings Charlotta the Fourth and I often sit out here and amuse ourselves with them. Charlotta, take back the horn and hang it carefully in its place."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "It gave me a shock to hear about Stephen’s son that first day you were here, Anne. I’ve never been able to mention him to you since, but I’ve wanted to know all about him. What sort of a boy is he?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "Oh, I’m not so old as I thought . . . and I don’t need a single blue pill! Girls, when you come back with your strawberries we’ll have tea out here under the silver poplar. I’ll have it all ready for you with home-grown cream."

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert grew up at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert grew up at Green Gables, where she spent sixty years leading an easy, conservative life alongside her brother Matthew. In her youth, she quarreled with John Blythe and refused to forgive him when he asked, a choice she would later look back on with quiet regret. Her life took a major turn when she and Matthew decided to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, only for a mix-up to bring a young girl, Anne Shirley, to Green Gables instead. Though initially determined to send the child back, Marilla was moved by pity for Anne's neglected past and agreed to raise her, taking full responsibility for the girl's upbringing and discipline. Over the years, Marilla found her strict principles tested and softened by Anne's imaginative mishaps, growing to love the girl deeply and feeling immense pride as Anne excelled academically. Following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack, Marilla grieved alongside Anne, only to learn shortly after that her own failing eyesight threatened to force the sale of Green Gables. However, Anne sacrificed her college scholarship to stay home, teach locally, and care for Marilla. To enable Anne to eventually attend Redmond College, Marilla invited the newly widowed Mrs. Rachel Lynde to move into Green Gables, and later agreed to permanently raise the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. As the years passed, Marilla continued to manage the bustling household, offering a steady home for Anne during her holiday breaks and life milestones.

unit: Marilla Cuthbert grew up at Green Gables, where she spent sixty years leading an easy, conservative life alongside her brother Matthew. In her youth, she quarreled with John Blythe and refused to forgive him when he asked, a choice she would later look back on with quiet regret. Her life took a major turn when she and Matthew decided to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, only for a mix-up to bring a young girl, Anne Shirley, to Green Gables instead. Though initially determined to send the child back, Marilla was moved by pity for Anne's neglected past and agreed to raise her, taking full responsibility for the girl's upbringing and discipline. Over the years, Marilla found her strict principles tested and softened by Anne's imaginative mishaps, growing to love the girl deeply and feeling immense pride as Anne excelled academically. Following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack, Marilla grieved alongside Anne, only to learn shortly after that her own failing eyesight threatened to force the sale of Green Gables. However, Anne sacrificed her college scholarship to stay home, teach locally, and care for Marilla. To enable Anne to eventually attend Redmond College, Marilla invited the newly widowed Mrs. Rachel Lynde to move into Green Gables, and later agreed to permanently raise the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. As the years passed, Marilla continued to manage the bustling household, offering a steady home for Anne during her holiday breaks and life milestones.

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "No. We want a boy to help Matthew on the farm. A girl would be of no use to us. Take off your hat. I’ll lay it and your bag on the hall table."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "Well, undress as quick as you can and go to bed. I’ll come back in a few minutes for the candle. I daren’t trust you to put it out yourself. You’d likely set the place on fire."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "I suppose we could, but we decided not to. Matthew took a fancy to her. And I must say I like her myself—although I admit she has her faults. The house seems a different place already. She’s a real bright little thing."

Refusing to leave her behind, he brought her home and quietly advocated for keeping her despite Marilla's initial reluctance. He later secretly visited Anne during a punishment to gently persuade her to apologize to Mrs. Rachel Lynde, and he frequently showed his support for her, such as bringing her chocolates and warm encouragement. When Anne was saving up to buy a flag at school, Matthew went behind Marilla's back to enlist Mrs. Lynde's help in getting Anne a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas.

label: History
value: Matthew willingly agreed to pay for Anne's extra studies in the Queen's Entrance class
unit: As Anne grew older, Matthew willingly agreed to pay for her extra studies in the Queen's Entrance class so she could train to become a teacher. Despite facing failing health, he took great pride in Anne's academic triumphs, including her tying for first place on the entrance exams and later winning the Avery scholarship at Queen's Academy. During Anne's return home to Avonlea, Matthew spent a peaceful day walking with her and tenderly expressed how proud he was of her. Shortly afterward, Matthew suffered a fatal collapse and died suddenly after reading a newspaper report detailing the failure of the Abbey Bank.

label: History
value: Paul Irving was a young student.
unit: Paul Irving was a young student who instantly formed a close bond with his teacher, Anne, on her first day at the Avonlea schoolhouse. Imaginative by nature, he frequently shared fantastical stories about his fictional shore friends and wrote creative compositions, such as a piece describing a moonshine boat. Three years after the death of his mother, who used to sit with him until he fell asleep, Paul spoke openly with Anne about his memories of her and his inner thoughts. Through Anne, Paul met Miss Lavendar at Echo Lodge and quickly formed a sweet bond of mutual understanding with her while discussing her imaginary dream-boy. When Paul's father, Stephen Irving, arrived in town, Anne helped reunite him with Miss Lavendar, leading to their wedding and leaving the local community buzzing over the romance.

value: Paul Irving said: "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes . . . the look my little mother always had. I think it’s a pity you haven’t any boys of your own."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "you can’t think what has happened! Something so splendid. Father is here . . . just think of that! Father is here! Come right in. Father, this is my beautiful teacher. You know, father."

value: Paul Irving said: “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon grew up attending church.
unit: Philippa "Phil" Gordon, the daughter of a prominent, wealthy man from an exclusive Bluenose family in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, grew up attending church—where her grandmother would give her peppermints—and once spent an entire summer teaching a Sunday school class. After enrolling at Redmond College in Kingsport, she first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant while wandering through Old St. John's Cemetery. An exuberant and talkative student torn between two suitors, Alec and Alonzo, Phil quickly became close friends with Anne and Priscilla, later enthusiastically begging to move into Patty's Place with them, Stella, and Aunt Jamesina for their sophomore year. Over the summer, while staying at a boarding house in Prospect Point, Phil met an ugly but earnest divinity student named Jonas Blake and unexpectedly fell in love with him. Upon returning to college, she announced her engagement to Jonas, happily embracing a future as a minister's wife in the slums. During their time at Redmond, Phil frequently offered commentary on Anne's romantic prospects and kept her informed of college gossip regarding Gilbert Blythe and Christine Stuart. Shortly after graduating from Redmond, Phil married Jonas in her hometown of Bolingbroke with Anne in attendance.

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I’ll go, if I can walk with Priscilla and Charlie. That will be a bearable degree of gooseberry. That Gilbert of yours is a darling, Anne, but why does he go around so much with Goggle-eyes?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I don’t want William’s Island especially, but I’m sure I couldn’t get it if I did. Look at that sentry on the summit of the fort, right beside the flag. Doesn’t he look as if he had stepped out of a romance?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Look—in white letters, around the archway over the gate. ‘Patty’s Place.’ Isn’t that killing? Especially on this Avenue of Pinehursts and Elmwolds and Cedarcrofts? ‘Patty’s Place,’ if you please! I adore it."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "They really are such dear boys, you know. There’s to be no end of dances and drives and general jamborees. I shall never forgive you, Queen Anne, for not coming home with me for the holidays."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "There’ll be one or two quilting parties, I suppose; and all the old gossips will talk you over to your face and behind your back. You’ll die of lonesomeness, child."

label: History
value: Phillips served as the schoolmaster in Avonlea.
unit: Phillips served as the schoolmaster in Avonlea, having originally secured the position because his uncle was a school trustee, and he boarded at Eben Wright's house. Known for maintaining poor order in his classroom while frequently whipping his pupils, he publicly humiliated Anne Shirley on her first day back by forcing her to stand at the blackboard and later making her sit with Gilbert Blythe as punishment for her tardiness. Following these incidents, Phillips eventually departed from his role as the village schoolmaster.

label: Personality
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an exceptionally capable woman.
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an exceptionally capable woman and a clever manager who effortlessly handles her own affairs as well as those of others. Known throughout Avonlea as a red-hot politician, she is a shrewd judge of human nature, highly observant, and very farseeing, though she holds decided prejudices against anyone born outside of Prince Edward Island. Characterized as an outspoken, bossy, and somewhat officious gossip, she takes pride in speaking her mind, often nagging people to do right and finding fault with those around her. Despite her critical, practical, and sometimes pessimistic nature—alongside a firm belief in foreordination and a dark dubiousness toward writing fiction—she possesses a truly kind heart, genuine generosity, and a willingness to help the poor. As a devout church member, she considers horse racing an abomination and strictly avoids it to set a good religious example.

unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived as Marilla Cuthbert's neighbor for forty-five years, having married when she was eighteen and previously had a husband who was cheated out of ten dollars in Boston. After raising ten children who went to school, she visited Green Gables to express skepticism upon learning Matthew and Marilla intended to adopt an orphan boy. When a young girl named Anne Shirley arrived instead, Mrs. Lynde visited and insulted her appearance, provoking a furious outburst from Anne before eventually receiving a dramatic apology and forgiving her. Later, when Anne refused to return to school after a humiliation, Mrs. Lynde advised Marilla to let the girl stay home until she cooled off. She assisted Matthew by making a new dress with puffed sleeves for Anne for Christmas, and later praised Anne's beauty and growth to Marilla. Following the sudden death of her husband, Thomas, Mrs. Lynde accepted Marilla's invitation to move to Green Gables, allowing Anne to leave her teaching job and attend Redmond College. label: History
value: Roy Gardner left college.
unit: Roy Gardner left college and went abroad with his mother after her health failed. Two years later, he rescued Anne Shirley during a rainstorm, walked her home, and sent her roses, initiating a romance with her. Over the course of their time together at Redmond College, he escorted her to events and eventually introduced her to his family, with his sister Dorothy bonding warmly with Anne. However, at the harbor pavilion, Roy proposed to Anne, only for her to realize she did not love him and reject his proposal, effectively ending their relationship.

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "That ought to be sufficient introduction. My name is Royal Gardner. And you are the Miss Shirley who read the Tennyson paper at the Philomathic the other evening, aren’t you?"

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "I feel as if I didn’t belong anywhere yet. I put in my Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond two years ago. I’ve been in Europe ever since. Now I’ve come back to finish my Arts course."

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "I can’t understand it—I can’t believe you are not the woman I’ve believed you to be. But reproaches are idle between us. You are the only woman I can ever love. I thank you for your friendship, at least. Good-bye, Anne."

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "So we are classmates as well as collegemates. I am reconciled to the loss of the years that the locust has eaten"

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "Pardon me—may I offer you the shelter of my umbrella?"

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea
unit: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea with many big sisters and once had her warts magically charmed away by old Mary Joe from the Creek. During her schooldays, she joined Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews in forming a Story Club. She later went on a visit to Boston during the autumn and eventually received a marriage proposal from Nelson Atkins. While Anne was away at Redmond College, Ruby maintained correspondence with Gilbert Blythe. Upon returning home, Anne learned that Ruby was terminally ill. During a visit, Ruby attempted to keep up a lively facade regarding her social life and future plans, but she later tearfully confessed her fear of dying and her love for her earthly life to Anne. Ruby passed away peacefully in her sleep the following night, leaving Anne and the Avonlea community to mourn her.

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: “Nor I,” said Ruby Gillis, with a shiver. “I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright.”

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "There’s a concert at Carmody and a party at White Sands. Herb Spencer’s going to take me. He’s my latest. Be sure to come up tomorrow. I’m dying for a good talk with you. I want to hear all about your doings at Redmond."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Me! Why, I’m perfectly well. I never felt better in my life. Of course, that congestion last winter pulled me down a little. But just see my color. I don’t look much like an invalid, I’m sure."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Anne, it won’t be long now before I’ll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I’ll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: “I know it—I’ve known it all summer, though I wouldn’t give in. And, oh, Anne”—she reached out and caught Anne’s hand pleadingly, impulsively—“I don’t want to die. I’m afraid to die.”

value: Rusty was a stray cat.
unit: Rusty was a stray cat who unexpectedly adopted Anne Shirley during her sophomore year at Redmond, remaining with her at Patty's Place after a failed attempt by the girls to humanely euthanize him. Upon the arrival of Aunt Jamesina's pets, Rusty attempted to assert dominance over the household's new animals; he was swiftly defeated by the Sarah-cat and engaged in ongoing skirmishes with Joseph until the two eventually became friends. He also engaged in a pitched battle where he routed the tobacco-king's cat.

label: History
value: Twenty years prior, Sarah was prevented by her father from marrying Luther Wallace.
unit: Twenty years prior, Sarah was prevented by her father from marrying Luther Wallace because he was poor, leading her to whitewash her duckhouse every spring in case it might be needed. Years later, she rescued Anne Shirley when Anne crashed through her duckhouse roof while trying to look for a blue willow-ware platter. Sarah hosted Anne and Diana for tea, complained about her sister Martha, and agreed to sell the platter to Anne for twenty-five dollars to help fund her upcoming marriage. Later, a cat named the Sarah-cat, who had been given to Aunt Jamesina by her washerwoman, lived alongside Joseph and Rusty at Patty's Place.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley endured a neglected childhood living with different families and at an asylum before being brought to Avonlea. value: Shirley said: "In the years to come thy memory will shine like a star over my lonely life, as that last story we read together says. Diana, wilt thou give me a lock of thy jet-black tresses in parting to treasure forevermore?"

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: "That is all there is left in life for me, now that my friend has been ruthlessly torn from me. In school I can look at her and muse over days departed."

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: "I’d be able to help you so much now and spare you in a hundred ways. I could find it in my heart to wish I had been, just for that."

label: History
value: Miss Stacy was hired as Avonlea's first female schoolteacher.
unit: Miss Stacy was hired as Avonlea's first female schoolteacher, maintaining perfect order among her pupils without ever resorting to corporal punishment. Upon her arrival, she quickly became a popular and encouraging figure who introduced field afternoons and organized a student Christmas concert to raise money for a schoolhouse flag. Recognizing the potential in her students, she visited Green Gables to propose organizing an advanced class to prepare Anne and others for the Queen's Entrance examination. She spent the following years mentoring the class through their studies, and upon the end of her term, she shared an emotional farewell with her students before Anne went on to tie for first place on the exam.

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "And now, Anne, I’ve a little plan. You know how I loathe boarding. I’ve boarded for four years and I’m so tired of it. I don’t feel like enduring three years more of it."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I was afraid they’d come back. And then our jolly little nest here would be broken up—and we poor callow nestlings thrown out on the cruel world of boardinghouses again."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I love Anne and I like Roy. Everybody says she is making a brilliant match, and even Mrs. Gardner thinks her charming now. It all sounds as if it were made in heaven, but I have my doubts. Make the most of that, Aunt Jamesina."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "As to the financial part—but I’ll not begin on that. Those whom the gods wish to destroy they first make country schoolmarms!"

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Nothing seems worthwhile. My very thoughts are old. I’ve thought them all before. What is the use of living after all, Anne?"

chapter: v2 · V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am
unit: Anne begins her first day teaching at the schoolhouse, where she forgets her prepared speech but quietly observes her pupils, bonding instantly with young Paul Irving. After dealing with minor classroom disruptions and a visit from the eccentric Mrs. Donnell regarding her children's names, Anne receives orchids from Paul on her walk home. Later at Green Gables, Marilla and Mrs. Lynde discuss the day's events, including Anthony Pye's stubborn dislike of Anne.

value: Diana helps Anne dress
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert
unit: Diana helps Anne dress at Green Gables for a benefit concert at the White Sands Hotel, while Marilla looks on with quiet pride. Billy Andrews drives Anne, Diana, and Jane to the hotel, where Anne initially experiences severe stage fright upon seeing the sophisticated crowd and accomplished performers. However, catching sight of Gilbert Blythe sparks her determination, leading her to deliver a glowing recitation that wins enthusiastic applause and praise from the audience.

unit: Anne and Mr. Harrison discuss Mrs. Lynde and the village improvement projects, including the plan to paint the local hall green. value: Anne puts Davy to bed.

unit: Anne puts Davy to bed and chats with him before Diana signals her to come over with news of a potential replacement willow-ware platter at the Copp place. The next day, Anne and Diana drive to Spencervale to search for the platter, but upon finding the Copp home empty, Anne climbs onto a small duck house to peek into the pantry window. She crashes through the roof and gets trapped, having to wait through a rainstorm until Miss Sarah Copp returns and releases her with an axe, after which Miss Sarah offers to sell her the platter over tea.

value: Marilla leaves for town.
chapter: v2 · XX The Way It Often Happens
unit: Marilla leaves for town while Anne stays home and handles chores, including transferring feathers between ticks, which leaves her covered in fluff. Mistaking a bottle of dye for her freckle lotion, Anne accidentally colors her nose bright red right before Priscilla Grant unexpectedly arrives with famous author Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. After quickly washing off the dye, Anne and Diana host the distinguished guests for a pleasant meal and a stroll through the local sights before they depart.

unit: Anne returns to teaching, dealing with schoolroom antics from Davy and comforting Dora after Mirabel Cotton frightens her with ghost stories. Later, Anne and Diana set out to walk to a tea party in West Grafton, but accidentally wander down an enchanted wood lane that leads them to Echo Lodge, the home of Miss Lavendar Lewis. Miss Lavendar warmly invites the lost girls inside to join her for a tea party she had been playfully imagining by herself.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Anne and Gilbert joke about their anonymous newspaper prank.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Anne and Gilbert joke about their anonymous newspaper prank and Uncle Abe's storm prediction, but an extraordinarily severe hail and thunder storm strikes Avonlea on that exact date. The storm destroys crops, damages homes, kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger, and wrecks the trees planted by the Improvers. Afterwards, the community recovers and assesses the widespread damage, while Gilbert and Anne resolve to replant their lost trees next spring.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana return from a shopping trip in Carmody discussing plans for the Avonlea Improvement Society. Upon seeing a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's oat field, Anne mistakenly assumes it is her own mischievous cow, chases it out with Diana's help, and impulsively sells it to Mr. Shearer. After arriving home, Anne discovers her real cow Dolly in the barnyard and realizes she sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to set off to apologize to him with a nut cake peace offering.

value: Anne puts Davy to bed.
chapter: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
unit: Anne puts Davy to bed and chats with him before Diana signals her to come over with news of a potential replacement willow-ware platter at the Copp place. The next day, Anne and Diana drive to Spencervale to search for the platter, but upon finding the Copp home empty, Anne climbs onto a small duck house to peek into the pantry window. She crashes through the roof and gets trapped, having to wait through a rainstorm until Miss Sarah Copp returns and releases her with an axe, after which Miss Sarah offers to sell her the platter over tea.

unit: Marilla leaves for town while Anne stays home and handles chores, including transferring feathers between ticks, which leaves her covered in fluff. Mistaking a bottle of dye for her freckle lotion, Anne accidentally colors her nose bright red right before Priscilla Grant unexpectedly arrives with famous author Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. After quickly washing off the dye, Anne and Diana host the distinguished guests for a pleasant meal and a stroll through the local sights before they depart.

unit: Anne returns to teaching, dealing with schoolroom antics from Davy and comforting Dora after Mirabel Cotton frightens her with ghost stories. unit: Anne and Diana rest after picking apples and reflect on how much their lives and community are changing as they grow older and prepare to leave for college. She returns to Green Gables to comfort Davy Keith before slipping away to Victoria Island to escape her troubles in daydreaming.

However, they accidentally jump onto a sleeping Aunt Josephine in the spare-room bed, infuriating her. Upon learning the next day that Aunt Josephine plans to leave and cancel Diana's music lessons, Anne feels deeply remorseful for causing trouble.

unit: Anne and her friends attempt to reenact the story of Elaine in a flat boat on the pond, but the boat begins to leak, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Afterward, back at Green Gables, Marilla despairs over Anne's antics while Matthew quietly encourages her to keep a little of her romance.

unit: Anne, Jane, and Gilbert discuss their upcoming teaching roles and debate whether corporal punishment is effective or necessary in maintaining order. The next morning, a nervous Anne shares her fears of failure with Marilla before starting her first day as a schoolteacher.

unit: Anne and Diana continue canvassing Avonlea for the Improvement Society, encountering various eccentric neighbors, including a remarkably tidy woman and a father celebrating the birth of his new son. unit: Gilbert visits Anne and the two discuss their teaching experiences, literary ambitions, and future career plans. label: v2 · IX A Question of Color
value: Anne and Mr. Harrison discuss Mrs. Lynde
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne and Mr. Harrison discuss Mrs. Lynde and the village improvement projects, including the plan to paint the local hall green. However, due to a mix-up with the paint numbers, Joshua Pye paints the hall a glaring bright blue with a red roof. Although the village is initially shocked by the hideous result, public sympathy shifts in favor of the Improvers against the Pyes.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Anne walks home with Mrs. Lynde
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Anne walks home with Mrs. Lynde, discussing community news and preparations for an upcoming bazaar. At home, Marilla receives a letter from the twins' uncle postponing his taking them, after which Anne remembers a past conversation with Davy following his jam-stealing episode. Later, at an Improvement Society meeting, the members are outraged to learn that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence for advertisements, and a committee sent to reason with him returns unsuccessful.

chapter: v2 · XV The Beginning of Vacation
unit: Anne completes her school year and walks to the Avonlea cemetery to tend Matthew's grave. Along the way, she talks with Paul Irving about his mother, imagination, and school life. At the graveyard, after placing flowers on Matthew's and Hester Gray's graves, Anne meets Mrs. Allan and they walk home together discussing teaching, future goals, and friendship.

value: Anne and Gilbert joke about their anonymous newspaper prank.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Anne and Gilbert joke about their anonymous newspaper prank and Uncle Abe's storm prediction, but an extraordinarily severe hail and thunder storm strikes Avonlea on that exact date. The storm destroys crops, damages homes, kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger, and wrecks the trees planted by the Improvers. Afterwards, the community recovers and assesses the widespread damage, while Gilbert and Anne resolve to replant their lost trees next spring.

She returns to Green Gables to comfort Davy Keith before slipping away to Victoria Island to escape her troubles in daydreaming.

chapter: v3 · Chapter II Garlands of Autumn
unit: The Avonlea Young People's Improvement Society hosts a farewell party for Anne and Gilbert before they leave for college, presenting them with tokens of appreciation. Anne is annoyed by Gilbert's sentimental remark during supper and accepts Charlie Sloane's escort home, which leaves her regretting her choice. The following evening, after receiving well-meaning but discouraging comments from local women about attending Redmond, Anne takes a long walk with Gilbert through the woods where they find a wild apple tree and rekindle their comfortable companionship.

unit: Anne and Diana return from a shopping trip in Carmody discussing plans for the Avonlea Improvement Society. Upon seeing a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's oat field, Anne mistakenly assumes it is her own mischievous cow, chases it out with Diana's help, and impulsively sells it to Mr. Shearer. After arriving home, Anne discovers her real cow Dolly in the barnyard and realizes she sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to set off to apologize to him with a nut cake peace offering.

chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Anne and Gilbert joke about their anonymous newspaper prank and Uncle Abe's storm prediction, but an extraordinarily severe hail and thunder storm strikes Avonlea on that exact date. The storm destroys crops, damages homes, kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger, and wrecks the trees planted by the Improvers. Afterwards, the community recovers and assesses the widespread damage, while Gilbert and Anne resolve to replant their lost trees next spring.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: Anne is humiliated by Mr. Phillips at school, first by being made to stand in front of the blackboard and later by being forced to sit with Gilbert Blythe after arriving late. Outraged, Anne vows never to return to school or forgive Gilbert, ignoring his attempts to apologize. Marilla seeks advice from Rachel Lynde, who recommends letting Anne stay home until she cools off, while Anne continues to study at home and dramatically frets over her future friendship with Diana.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends attempt to reenact the story of Elaine in a flat boat on the pond, but the boat begins to leak, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne cold-shoulders his offer to end their feud. Afterward, back at Green Gables, Marilla despairs over Anne's antics while Matthew quietly encourages her to keep a little of her romance.

unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in town, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together at Green Gables. unit: Anne and Diana return from a shopping trip in Carmody discussing plans for the Avonlea Improvement Society. Upon seeing a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's oat field, Anne mistakenly assumes it is her own mischievous cow, chases it out with Diana's help, and impulsively sells it to Mr. Shearer. After arriving home, Anne discovers her real cow Dolly in the barnyard and realizes she sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to set off to apologize to him with a nut cake peace offering.

After being punished for his antics, Davy confesses to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

unit: Anne and Mr. Harrison discuss Mrs. Lynde and the village improvement projects, including the plan to paint the local hall green. However, due to a mix-up with the paint numbers, Joshua Pye paints the hall a glaring bright blue with a red roof. Although the village is initially shocked by the hideous result, public sympathy shifts in favor of the Improvers against the Pyes.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Anne and Gilbert joke about their anonymous newspaper prank.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Anne and Gilbert joke about their anonymous newspaper prank and Uncle Abe's storm prediction, but an extraordinarily severe hail and thunder storm strikes Avonlea on that exact date. The storm destroys crops, damages homes, kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger, and wrecks the trees planted by the Improvers. Afterwards, the community recovers and assesses the widespread damage, while Gilbert and Anne resolve to replant their lost trees next spring.

value: The Avonlea Young People's Improvement Society hosts a farewell party.
chapter: v3 · Chapter II Garlands of Autumn
unit: The Avonlea Young People's Improvement Society hosts a farewell party for Anne and Gilbert before they leave for college, presenting them with tokens of appreciation. Anne is annoyed by Gilbert's sentimental remark during supper and accepts Charlie Sloane's escort home, which leaves her regretting her choice. The following evening, after receiving well-meaning but discouraging comments from local women about attending Redmond, Anne takes a long walk with Gilbert through the woods where they find a wild apple tree and rekindle their comfortable companionship.

unit: In a terrible mood caused by a toothache, Anne has a disaster-filled day at school, accidentally exploding a package of firecrackers brought by a student before whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. After venting her shame and regret to Marilla at home, Anne is surprised the next morning when Anthony treats her with new respect. Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms that Anne has finally won Anthony over by giving him a proper whipping.

Before the girls depart, a slip of the tongue brings up Paul Irving's name, leaving Miss Lavendar visibly moved and quiet as she gives them lavendar and bids them farewell.

chapter: v3 · Chapter XXI Roses of Yesterday
unit: During her pleasant visit to Bolingbroke with Phil, Anne visits the small yellow house where she was born and learns more about her parents from the current resident. The woman hands Anne a bundle of old love letters written by her parents, which Anne reads reverently after visiting their grave. Reading the letters makes Anne feel truly connected to her parents for the first time in her life.

label: v3 · Chapter XXIV Enter Jonas
value: Philippa writes a long letter to Anne.
chapter: v3 · Chapter XXIV Enter Jonas
unit: Philippa writes a long letter to Anne from Prospect Point describing her summer spent at Cousin Emily's boarding house. She humorously introduces the eccentric fellow boarders and relates how she met Jonas Blake, a divinity student. Though she tries to deny her feelings because he is ugly and serious, Phil admits by the end of her letter that she has fallen in love with him.

chapter: v3 · Chapter XXVII Mutual Confidences
unit: As April examinations approach, the girls at Patty's Place prepare for their studies and learn that Miss Patty and Miss Maria will remain abroad for another year. Phil takes Anne for a evening walk in the park, where she joyfully reveals that she has accepted Jonas Blake's marriage proposal. As they discuss Phil's future as a minister's wife in the slums, Phil asks Anne about her feelings for Roy Gardner, prompting Anne to reflect on her ideal romance with Roy and her lingering thoughts of Gilbert Blythe.

label: v3 · Chapter XXXVII Full-fledged B.A.’s
value: The girls' and Aunt Jamesina's final examinations are coming to an end.
chapter: v3 · Chapter XXXVII Full-fledged B.A.’s
unit: As their final examinations come to an end, the girls and Aunt Jamesina reflect on what their four years at Redmond College have taught them. For Convocation and the graduation dance, Anne chooses to wear Gilbert's gifted lilies-of-the-valley and pink enamel heart pendant instead of Roy's violets. However, after Phil mentions a rumor about Gilbert's engagement to Christine Stuart, a hurt Anne snaps the necklace, turns Gilbert down for a dance, and masks her heartbreak during the night's festivities.

unit: Anne completes her second term at Redmond College while dealing with an unwanted marriage proposal from Charlie Sloane. unit: Anne and Priscilla visit Patty's Place to inquire about renting the house from Miss Patty Spofford and Miss Maria. label: v3 · Chapter XI The Round of Life
value: Anne returns to Avonlea.
chapter: v3 · Chapter XI The Round of Life
unit: Anne returns to Avonlea and notices changes in the community during Sunday church, including the marriage of Billy Andrews and news that Ruby Gillis is terminally ill. The next evening, Anne and Diana visit Aunt Atossa to drop off jelly before going to see Ruby. At the Gillis home, Ruby tries to maintain a lively facade about her social life and future plans despite her deteriorating health.

label: v3 · Chapter XIV The Summons
value: Anne visits Ruby Gillis.
chapter: v3 · Chapter XIV The Summons
unit: Anne visits a dying Ruby Gillis, who tearfully confesses her fear of death and her reluctance to leave the earthly life she loves. Anne offers gentle comfort and reflects deeply on life's true purpose as she walks home. The following night, Ruby passes away peacefully in her sleep, leaving Anne, Diana, Davy, and the Avonlea community to mourn her and reflect on her memory.

The following night, Ruby passes away peacefully in her sleep, leaving Anne, Diana, Davy, and the Avonlea community to mourn her and reflect on her memory.

chapter: v3 · Chapter XVI Adjusted Relationships
unit: Anne and her friends return to Redmond for their Sophomore year and settle comfortably into Patty’s Place. After Anne is unexpectedly adopted by a stray cat named Rusty, the girls fail to humane-euthanize him, and Anne decides to keep him. Aunt Jamesina arrives to chaperone the household, bringing along her own cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat.

unit: As April examinations approach, the girls at Patty's Place prepare for their studies and learn that Miss Patty and Miss Maria will remain abroad for another year. As they discuss Phil's future as a minister's wife in the slums, Phil asks Anne about her feelings for Roy Gardner, prompting Anne to reflect on her ideal romance with Roy and her lingering thoughts of Gilbert Blythe.

label: v3 · Chapter XXXVII Full-fledged B.A.’s
value: The girls' final examinations are coming to an end.
chapter: v3 · Chapter XXXVII Full-fledged B.A.’s
unit: As their final examinations come to an end, the girls and Aunt Jamesina reflect on what their four years at Redmond College have taught them. For Convocation and the graduation dance, Anne chooses to wear Gilbert's gifted lilies-of-the-valley and pink enamel heart pendant instead of Roy's violets. However, after Phil mentions a rumor about Gilbert's engagement to Christine Stuart, a hurt Anne snaps the necklace, turns Gilbert down for a dance, and masks her heartbreak during the night's festivities.

value: Anne and Diana bid a farewell to Miss Stacy
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
unit: Anne and Diana bid a emotional farewell to Miss Stacy at the end of the school term. Anne travels to town to take her Queen's Academy entrance examinations, detailing her nervous experiences in a letter to Diana. Weeks later, Diana brings the published pass list to Green Gables, revealing that Anne tied for first place on the entire Island, bringing immense pride to Matthew, Marilla, and Mrs. Lynde.

value: Marilla returns from the oculist.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road
unit: Marilla returns from the oculist with news that her failing eyesight will force her to sell Green Gables. Anne resolutely refuses to let the farm be sold and forfeits her scholarship to Redmond so she can stay home, care for Marilla, and teach local school. Mrs. Lynde reveals that Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea school so Anne could have it, prompting Anne to reconcile and become close friends with Gilbert.

chapter: v2 · I An Irate Neighbor
unit: Anne is interrupted while studying Virgil by her angry new neighbor, Mr. Harrison, who complains about her Jersey cow trespassing in his oats. After a sharp exchange, Anne pens up the cow and prepares tea for Marilla. They discuss farm affairs and are soon joined by Mrs. Rachel Lynde, who shares local gossip about incoming neighbors and future students.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana return from a shopping trip in Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana return from a shopping trip in Carmody discussing plans for the Avonlea Improvement Society. Upon seeing a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's oat field, Anne mistakenly assumes it is her own mischievous cow, chases it out with Diana's help, and impulsively sells it to Mr. Shearer. After arriving home, Anne discovers her real cow Dolly in the barnyard and realizes she sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to set off to apologize to him with a nut cake peace offering.

unit: Anne, Jane, and Gilbert discuss their upcoming teaching roles and debate whether corporal punishment is effective or necessary in maintaining order. Later, Anne walks past various local landmarks and visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to manage students through affection rather than discipline. The next morning, a nervous Anne shares her fears of failure with Marilla before starting her first day as a schoolteacher.

Although the village is initially shocked by the hideous result, public sympathy shifts in favor of the Improvers against the Pyes.

unit: Anne walks home from school feeling content and meets Diana along the Birch Path. When she arrives at Green Gables, Marilla informs her that Dora is missing, leading to a frantic search around the farm and well. Anne discovers that Davy locked Dora in Mr. Harrison's toolhouse and lied about it, but after a heart-to-heart conversation, she helps Davy understand the wrongness of lying before sending him to bed.

value: Anne has a terrible mood caused by a toothache.

unit: In a terrible mood caused by a toothache, Anne has a disaster-filled day at school, accidentally exploding a package of firecrackers brought by a student before whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. After venting her shame and regret to Marilla at home, Anne is surprised the next morning when Anthony treats her with new respect. Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms that Anne has finally won Anthony over by giving him a proper whipping.

After venting her shame and regret to Marilla at home, Anne is surprised the next morning when Anthony treats her with new respect. Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms that Anne has finally won Anthony over by giving him a proper whipping.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Anne walks home with Mrs. Lynde
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Anne walks home with Mrs. Lynde, discussing community news and preparations for an upcoming bazaar. At home, Marilla receives a letter from the twins' uncle postponing his taking them, after which Anne remembers a past conversation with Davy following his jam-stealing episode. Later, at an Improvement Society meeting, the members are outraged to learn that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence for advertisements, and a committee sent to reason with him returns unsuccessful.

Fearing Anne will expose the bribe, Judson quickly agrees to pull his advertising agreement, allowing Anne to announce to the Improvers that the fences are saved.

chapter: v2 · XIX Just a Happy Day
unit: Anne spends a pleasant late-August day rowing with Diana and the twins before visiting Paul Irving at his grandmother's house. Returning home to Green Gables, Anne puts a jealous Davy to bed and later meets Gilbert Blythe by the Dryad's Bubble.

value: Marilla leaves for town.
chapter: v2 · XX The Way It Often Happens
unit: Marilla leaves for town while Anne stays home and handles chores, including transferring feathers between ticks, which leaves her covered in fluff. Mistaking a bottle of dye for her freckle lotion, Anne accidentally colors her nose bright red right before Priscilla Grant unexpectedly arrives with famous author Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. After quickly washing off the dye, Anne and Diana host the distinguished guests for a pleasant meal and a stroll through the local sights before they depart.
